# Epic: Payment Conversion & Payment Experience

Coordinating issue for milestone **Payment Conversion & Payment Experience** (#99). Derived from the 2026-07-03 Stripe integration audit: the capability/UX roadmap — everything here improves buyer conversion or seller payout experience at **no major recurring cost** (no Stripe Tax, no Radar for Fraud Teams, no Instant Payouts). Companion milestone: #98 (Stripe Integration Hardening) carries the defects from the same audit.

## Intent
The funnel's biggest conversion losses are structural, not cosmetic:

1. **No wallets, no Link, anywhere.** Every session pins one `payment_method_types[0]` with `dynamicPaymentMethods: false`. Wallets and Link ride card rails — the existing card fee category already prices them; enabling them is mapping work, not fee-model work.
2. **Card entry after the commit point.** "Pay now" creates orders and redirects; the card form is the 6th section of the next page. The saved-instrument fast path (~2 clicks) proves the collapsed funnel works.
3. **Sellers get blocked and surprised.** Our readiness gate is stricter than Stripe's (`eventually_due` blocks payouts), restriction reasons are swallowed, and there is no warning before payouts pause.

## Findings → issues

**Buyer funnel — wallet/Link chain (serial where marked)**
- [ ] #3979 — Attach a Stripe Customer to every authenticated payment (Radar signal + Link prerequisite) — first
- [ ] #3980 — P1: Enable Apple Pay, Google Pay, and Link in the Payment Element (flagship) — after #3979; fee-category mapping stable regardless of the #3565 fee-number decision
- [ ] #3982 — Prefill Payment Element with buyer email/name/address (defaultValues) — feeds Link recognition; after m98 #3971 (same file)
- [ ] #3988 — Move card entry onto the checkout page ("Pay now" should pay) — structural, design-gated, lands last; after m89 checkout-page chain #3848→#3829→#3830

**Buyer funnel — independent quick wins**
- [ ] #3981 — statement_descriptor_suffix on all payments (dispute reduction)
- [ ] #3983 — Checkout address form: country select + autoComplete tokens — serial with m89 checkout-page chain
- [ ] #3984 — Embedded (not hosted-redirect) save-payment-method setup — after m98 #3975 (default semantics) and #3971
- [ ] #3985 — Payment page commit UX: sticky confirm bar, form prominence, reserved element height — rebase over m89 payout-leak fix

**Seller payout experience**
- [ ] #3986 — P1: Readiness semantics — stop blocking on eventually_due; surface disabled_reason + deadlines; posture-requirement grouping
- [ ] #3987 — notification_banner embedded component + readiness-regression email — after #3986 and m98 #3972 (CSP)

**Ops**
- [ ] #3989 — Stripe dashboard polish checklist: Connect branding, Apple Pay domain registration, statement prefix, payment-method configuration review — items 2/4 sequence with #3980

## Sequencing summary
Two serial chains: **element chain** m98 #3971 → #3974 → #3982 → #3984 → #3988 (same confirmation-card/checkout machinery), and **seller chain** #3986 → #3987. #3979 → #3980 gates the wallet work; #3980 needs the #3565 fee-number decision only for copy, not for category mapping. #3983 and #3988 both touch `checkout-page.tsx` — strictly serial with the m89 chain. Everything else parallelizes.

## Explicit non-goals (decided — do not re-open without new evidence)
- **Stripe Tax** — per tax posture: no collection until per-state economic nexus; nexus tracking is the near-term need, not calculation.
- **Radar for Fraud Teams / Adaptive Acceptance / network tokens** — base Radar is included and dashboard-configured (see #3989); the rest is automatic on eligible volume. No code.
- **Instant Payouts** — per-payout fee.
- **BNPL / local payment methods** — different (higher) fee economics; revisit post-launch with volume data. #3989 item 4 guards against accidental dashboard enablement.
- **Express Checkout Element** — deferred until #3988 lands; competes with the order-first architecture today.
- **Stripe receipt emails** — redundant with the in-house transactional-email projectors (better branded, already tested).
- **Stripe Address Element** — DS is the canonical UI source; the saved-address book works. #3983 fixes the form instead.
- **Hosted onboarding / Express dashboard for sellers** — removed by ADR 0006; embedded-only stands.
- **Element locale support** — site is effectively en-only; m97 is removing dead locales.
- **Checkout Session consent_collection** — the hand-rolled consent + `setup_future_usage=off_session` audit trail is arguably better; keep.

## Verified already-good (baseline to protect)
- Saved-instrument fast path (~2-click repeat purchase) with server-confirmed off-session PIs and consent metadata.
- Guest flow: guest-buyer actor, claim-after-payment via passkey/magic link, email-exists redirect, cart merge.
- DS-token → Appearance API theming with MutationObserver reactivity and documented provider boundary (`EMBEDDED_STRIPE_APPEARANCE.md`).
- Embedded Connect onboarding page: themed, loading/error/retry states, readiness panel, deep-link safety.

If further conversion findings surface during implementation, add issues under this milestone rather than expanding existing ones.

# Issue: Implementasi Payment API (`/payments`)

## Deskripsi Tugas
Buat branch baru dengan nama `feature/payment-api` dan implementasikan fitur CRUD API untuk model `Payment` dengan menggunakan standar arsitektur NestJS. Validasi input harus menggunakan Zod dan sesuai dengan schema Prisma. Semua API di-protect menggunakan JWT Guard dan Role Guard.

## Role & Akses (RBAC)

Berikut adalah daftar endpoint beserta Role Guard yang harus dipasang:

| Method | Endpoint | Keterangan | Akses (Role) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `POST` | `/payments` | Create payment baru | `USER`, `ADMIN` |
| `GET` | `/payments` | List semua data payment | `ADMIN` (Jika `USER` hanya bisa melihat data payment miliknya sendiri) |
| `GET` | `/payments/:id` | Mengambil detail payment berdasarkan ID | `ADMIN`, atau `USER` (jika `payment.userId == req.user.id`) |
| `PATCH`| `/payments/:id` | Update data payment | `ADMIN` |
| `DELETE`|`/payments/:id` | Hapus data payment | `ADMIN` |

---

## Tahapan Implementasi untuk Programmer / AI

Berikut adalah panduan langkah demi langkah implementasi (step-by-step) mulai dari validasi sampai testing:

### 1. Persiapan Branch Baru
- Buat dan pindah ke branch baru bernama `feature/payment-api`.
- (Opsional) Generate module, controller, dan service menggunakan Nest CLI.

### 2. Implementasi DTO (Data Transfer Object) dengan Zod
- Buat file `create-payment.dto.ts` dan `update-payment.dto.ts` di folder `src/modules/payment/dto/`.
- Validasi data POST (`CreatePaymentDto`) dengan schema berikut (sesuai file `prisma/schema.prisma`):
  - `orderId`: `number` (Wajib, nilai positif)
  - `transactionId`: `string` (Wajib, minimal 1 karakter)
  - `amount`: `number` atau `string` decimal (Wajib, lebih dari 0)
  - `paymentMethod`: Enum `TRANSFER` | `E_WALLET` (Wajib)
  - `status`: Enum `PENDING` | `SETTLEMENT` | `FAILED` | `CANCELED` | `REFUNDED` (Opsional, default `PENDING`)
  - `paymentProof`: `string` URL (Opsional)
  - `metadata`: `object` JSON (Opsional)
- Validasi PATCH (`UpdatePaymentDto`) semua opsional (Partial dari `CreatePaymentDto`), dengan tambahan field:
  - `failureReason`: `string` (Opsional)
  - `refundAmount`: `number` (Opsional)
  - `refundedAt`: `date/string` datetime (Opsional)

### 3. Implementasi Service (`payment.service.ts`)
- **`create`**: Menerima DTO dan inject `userId` dari *request token*. Simpan data menggunakan `prisma.payment.create()`. (Penting: Pastikan `orderId` ada, dan valid milik user tersebut jika rolenya `USER`).
- **`findAll`**: Mengambil data list payment. Jika rolenya `ADMIN`, kembalikan semua payment. Jika `USER`, filter data berdasarkan `userId`.
- **`findById`**: Mencari payment berdasarkan ID. Jika payment tidak ada, throw `NotFoundException`. Jika rolenya `USER` dan bukan pemiliknya, throw `ForbiddenException` atau `NotFoundException`.
- **`update`**: Mengupdate data payment. Harus ada pengecekan keberadaan payment. Update via `prisma.payment.update()`.
- **`remove`**: Menghapus payment. Harus mengecek apakah ID payment ada sebelum di-delete via `prisma.payment.delete()`.

### 4. Implementasi Controller (`payment.controller.ts`)
- Tambahkan decorator `@UseGuards(JwtAccessAuthGuard, RoleGuard)` di tingkat *class* (Controller).
- Endpoint `POST /payments`:
  - Gunakan decorator `@Roles('USER', 'ADMIN')`
  - Ambil `req.user` untuk mengambil informasi role dan `userId`.
  - Format output memakai standar response service.
- Endpoint `GET /payments`:
  - Gunakan decorator `@Roles('USER', 'ADMIN')`
  - Teruskan data `req.user` ke Service untuk difilter (Admin melihat semua, User melihat miliknya saja).
- Endpoint `GET /payments/:id`:
  - Gunakan decorator `@Roles('USER', 'ADMIN')`
  - Menerima ID parameter dan mengembalikan data detail payment.
- Endpoint `PATCH /payments/:id`:
  - Gunakan decorator `@Roles('ADMIN')`
  - Menerima ID parameter dan payload body update.
- Endpoint `DELETE /payments/:id`:
  - Gunakan decorator `@Roles('ADMIN')`
  - Menghapus payment berdasarkan ID.

### 5. Registrasi Module
- Pastikan `PaymentModule` di-import dan terdaftar di `app.module.ts`.

### 6. Pengujian (Testing)
- **Unit Testing**: Buat `payment.service.spec.ts` dan `payment.controller.spec.ts` untuk menguji business logic secara isolasi (dengan menggunakan mock `PrismaService`).
- **E2E Testing**: Tambahkan test bed di `test/app.e2e-spec.ts` (Mocking) dan `test/app-real.e2e-spec.ts` (Real DB).
  - Test endpoint success untuk Admin & User.
  - Test validasi (zod validation error jika parameter kurang).
  - Test Role Access Control (misalnya memastikan user dengan role `USER` mendapatkan response `403 Forbidden` jika mencoba mengakses endpoint `PATCH` atau `DELETE`).
- **Manual Testing**: Buat file konfigurasi REST (contoh: `http/payments.http`) agar bisa dites melalui extension REST Client.

### 7. Dokumentasi
- Update file `README.md` dengan dokumentasi rute (route) API `/payments` yang baru saja dibuat.

### Selesai
Setelah seluruh unit dan end-to-end test lolos/hijau (passing), commit perubahan dan buatkan Pull Request (PR).

# Payment page commit UX: sticky confirm bar, payment-form prominence, reserved element height

Part of milestone **Payment Conversion & Payment Experience** (#99). From the 2026-07-03 Stripe integration audit.

## Context
The payment page is the highest-stakes step but has the weakest commit UX:
- It uses `CheckoutLayout` (`account-payment-page.tsx:67`) — not the `CheckoutFlowShell` + `CheckoutStickyActionBar` + `CheckoutMobileSummaryDisclosure` trio the checkout page uses — so on mobile "Confirm payment" is inline mid-page below six sections while one page earlier "Pay now" was sticky.
- The payment form is the **6th** `PageSection` down (`account-payment-page.tsx:306-327`); the page leads with a status timeline and fee breakdown instead of the thing the buyer came to do.
- The element mount (`MountPoint purpose="provider"`, `packages/design-system/src/primitives/layout.tsx:968`) reserves no min-height → iframe-load layout shift exactly where the user is about to type, with no skeleton.

## What to do
Adopt the checkout page's shell trio here; reorder so payment entry is the primary above-the-fold content (timeline/fee breakdown demoted to disclosure/summary); add a skeleton + reserved min-height on the provider mount.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Confirm CTA is sticky on mobile, consistent with the checkout page.
- [ ] Payment form visible without scrolling on mobile viewport (m76 breakpoints).
- [ ] No layout shift on element load (skeleton reserves height).

## Constraints
- DS-first: use existing shell primitives, no custom overrides; buyer payout-leak removal on this page is m89's — don't duplicate, rebase over it.
- Sibling worktree; `verify:static` + scoped payments tests before push; rebase onto latest main right before pushing.

_From reliability audit (deployed commit `8d984661`)._ Corroborated by two independent finders.

**Defect:** A payment broadcast just before expiry that confirms just after is never credited: watchers filter `expires_at > NOW()` (`bitcoin_watcher.rs:191`, `db/invoices.rs:281`) so polling stops, GC expires the row (`expire_invoices_past_deadline`), and `record_invoice_payment` is never called — its `expired→underpaid` branch (`invoices.rs:696`) is dead via the watcher path.

**Fix:** Introduce `payment_grace_secs`: watchers poll until `expires_at + grace`; GC expires only past `expires_at + grace`. The existing `expired→underpaid` credit branch then becomes reachable.

**Verify:** integration — pay near expiry, confirm within grace → credited; confirm past grace → stays expired.

## Parent

Parent PRD: #40

## What to build

Implement real source-compatible VNPAY payment handling for pending bookings. Payment creation returns a signed VNPAY URL, active attempts are reused safely, callbacks update payment/booking state exactly once, late successful provider results are isolated for manual reconciliation, and mail/payment-event side effects run after the database transaction commits.

This issue must not fake successful payments in the running backend.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Payment creation is available for owned payable PENDING bookings, rejects non-owned/non-pending/expired bookings correctly, and returns paymentId, merchantTxnRef, and paymentUrl inside the Spring envelope.
- [ ] The Vite payment creation adapter can post an empty body; Spring defaults locale to vn and only passes bankCode when provided.
- [ ] Merchant refs use BK_bookingUuid_epochMillis, are unique, and are used as vnp_TxnRef.
- [ ] VNPAY signing and verification match the documented source algorithm, including parameter filtering, sorting, encoding, HMAC-SHA512, and case-insensitive hash comparison.
- [ ] Payment URL expiry is capped by the booking pending expiry and sent to VNPAY where supported.
- [ ] Repeated payment creation returns the existing active valid URL; expired/unsafe attempts are marked CANCELED with a PaymentEvent before a new attempt is created.
- [ ] Return and IPN callbacks record PaymentEvent rows for matched valid payments, lock by merchantTxnRef, and only the first valid terminal callback performs side effects.
- [ ] Normal success marks payment SUCCEEDED, confirms the booking, sends/logs success email after commit, and redirects/returns provider success as appropriate.
- [ ] Normal provider failure marks payment FAILED and records events without confirming the booking.
- [ ] Late success marks payment LATE_SUCCEEDED, does not confirm or re-reserve the booking, creates targeted admin reconciliation notifications and events, and maps frontend return status to requires_review.
- [ ] Invalid checksum/order/amount/duplicate callback responses follow the documented VNPAY RspCode and Message rules.
- [ ] Tests cover signing, URL creation/reuse, callback locking/idempotence, success, failure, duplicate callback, late success, invalid checksum/order/amount, and after-commit email event behavior.

- #44

body:
<!-- TITLE: Add real payments via Mercado Pago Checkout Pro (payments package) -->
<!-- LABELS: feature, cross-module, p1 -->

## Summary
APEX currently has a mock checkout: `POST /api/orders` creates an order but no money ever changes hands, and the frontend cart is a local-only Zustand store that never talks to the server. This issue introduces a real purchase/payment flow using **Mercado Pago (Checkout Pro)** — the store sells in BRL and needs Pix, boleto, cards and installments (parcelamento), and Mercado Pago is the highest-trust option for Brazilian buyers. The integration must go through a **provider-agnostic abstraction** in a new workspace package (`packages/payments`) so that Stripe (or another provider) can be added later without touching the API or app. Orders start as `pending` and only transition to `paid` when a verified webhook confirms payment approval.

## Type
feature

## Affected Modules
- `packages/payments` — **new package** (`apex-store-payments`)
- `packages/database` — new `Payment` model + migration
- `packages/api` — pay endpoint + payments webhook
- `packages/app` — real checkout flow, success/failure pages, server cart sync

Data flow: `app` → `POST /api/orders/:id/pay` → `payments` provider creates Checkout Pro preference → user pays on Mercado Pago → Mercado Pago → `POST /api/webhooks/payments` → `payments` parses/verifies event → `database` updates `Payment` + `Order.status` → `app` polls/refetches order on `/checkout/success`.

## Current Behaviour
- `POST /api/orders` (checkout) creates an order with no payment step; nothing charges the customer.
- The cart lives only in the browser: `packages/app/src/store/cartStore.ts` is a persisted Zustand store, and the fully typed `cartApi` in `packages/app/src/services/api.ts` is never called — so the server-side `Cart`/`CartItem` tables are unused and checkout cannot be validated against real stock.
- There is no `Payment` model, no payment provider integration, and no webhook endpoint.

## Expected Behaviour
- A logged-in user checks out, is redirected to Mercado Pago Checkout Pro, pays with Pix/boleto/card (with installments), and is returned to `/checkout/success` or `/checkout/failure`.
- The order becomes `paid` **only** via a signature-verified webhook — never from the client redirect.
- On rejection/expiry, reserved stock is restored and the order reflects the failure.
- With `PAYMENTS_PROVIDER=mock`, the entire flow works end-to-end locally and in tests with no Mercado Pago credentials.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] **Happy path (Pix and card):** the user completes checkout, pays via Pix or card (approved) on Checkout Pro, Mercado Pago notifies the webhook, and the API sets `Payment.status = approved` and `Order.status = paid`; the user sees the paid order on `/checkout/success`.
- [ ] **Rejection path:** when a payment is rejected or the preference expires, the webhook sets `Payment.status = rejected`, the order is cancelled, and the reserved stock for each `OrderItem` is restored to `Product.stock`.
- [ ] **Webhook signature validation:** `POST /api/webhooks/payments` verifies the Mercado Pago `x-signature` HMAC using `MERCADOPAGO_WEBHOOK_SECRET` against the raw request body; requests with a missing or invalid signature are rejected with `401` and produce no state changes.
- [ ] **Idempotent webhook processing:** duplicate/replayed notifications for the same payment event (Mercado Pago retries aggressively) are processed at most once — re-delivery returns `200` but does not double-update `Payment`/`Order` or restore stock twice (dedupe on `provider` + `externalId` + status transition).
- [ ] **Mock provider end-to-end:** with `PAYMENTS_PROVIDER=mock` and no Mercado Pago credentials set, `POST /api/orders/:id/pay` returns a checkout URL, the mock auto-approves, and the order reaches `paid` — covering dev and automated tests.
- [ ] Orders are created as `pending` and there is no code path that sets `paid` other than the webhook handler.
- [ ] The API never trusts `back_urls` redirects for payment state; `/checkout/success` refetches the order from `GET /api/orders/:id` to display status.
- [ ] The app cart is synced with the server cart API (`GET/POST/PUT/DELETE /api/cart...`) for authenticated users so checkout totals and stock are validated server-side.

## Technical Context

### New package — `packages/payments` (`apex-store-payments`)
A scaffold already exists on branch `claude/app-review-purchase-system-bp8j0l` with:
- `PaymentProvider` interface: `createCheckout(order) → { checkoutUrl, externalId }`, `getPayment(externalId)`, `parseWebhook(headers, rawBody) → PaymentEvent`
- Shared payment types/statuses (all money as integer cents)
- `MockPaymentProvider` (auto-approves, for dev/tests)
- `createPaymentProvider(config)` factory

See also `docs/payments.md` (same branch) for the full design.

**This issue's scope is the `MercadoPagoProvider` implementation plus wiring:**
- `createCheckout`: create a Checkout Pro preference (items, BRL amounts, `external_reference = orderId`, `back_urls` built from `APP_BASE_URL`, `notification_url`), return `init_point` as `checkoutUrl` and preference/payment id as `externalId`.
- `parseWebhook`: validate the `x-signature`/`x-request-id` HMAC with `MERCADOPAGO_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, fetch payment details via `getPayment` when the notification only carries an id, and normalize to the shared `PaymentEvent` shape (status: pending/approved/rejected/refunded, method, amount, raw payload).
- Register the provider in `createPaymentProvider(config)` keyed by `PAYMENTS_PROVIDER=mock|mercadopago`.
- The package is already in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` (`packages/*`) and the root build order; `api/` should consume it via `workspace:*` and a TS project reference (compiled like `database/` → CommonJS `dist/`).

### `packages/database`
- New `Payment` model: `id`, `orderId` (FK → `Order`), `provider`, `externalId`, `status` (`pending`/`approved`/`rejected`/`refunded`), `amount`, `method`, `raw` payload (JSONB), timestamps. Follow the existing Sequelize v6 TS pattern (`InferAttributes`/`InferCreationAttributes`, snake_case columns).
- New migration `migrations/2026XXXXXXXXXX-create-payments.js`; unique index on (`provider`, `external_id`) to support webhook idempotency.
- Association: `Order.hasMany(Payment)` in `src/models/index.ts`; re-export from `src/index.ts`.
- `Order.status` already supports `pending/paid/shipped/delivered/cancelled` — no change needed there.

### `packages/api`
- `POST /api/orders/:id/pay` [auth] — verifies the order belongs to `req.user`, is `pending`, then calls `provider.createCheckout(order)`, persists a `Payment` row (`status = pending`), and returns `{ checkoutUrl }`.
- `POST /api/webhooks/payments` (public, no JWT) — mounted with `express.raw({ type: 'application/json' })` **for this route only** (signature verification needs the raw body; register it before the global `express.json()` in `src/app.ts`). Calls `provider.parseWebhook(headers, rawBody)`, then in a transaction: update `Payment`, set `Order.status = paid` on approval, or cancel + restore stock on rejection/expiry. Must be idempotent (see acceptance criteria). Exclude this route from rate limiting or use a dedicated generous limiter so Mercado Pago retries are not dropped.
- New files: `src/routes/payments.ts` (or extend `src/routes/orders.ts`), `src/controllers/paymentController.ts`.
- New env vars in `.env.example`: `MERCADOPAGO_ACCESS_TOKEN`, `MERCADOPAGO_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `PAYMENTS_PROVIDER=mock|mercadopago`, `APP_BASE_URL` (for `back_urls`).

### `packages/app`
- `src/pages/Checkout.tsx`: call the real `ordersApi.checkout()` (`src/services/api.ts`) to create the order, then `POST /api/orders/:id/pay` and `window.location.assign(checkoutUrl)`.
- New pages: `src/pages/CheckoutSuccess.tsx` and `src/pages/CheckoutFailure.tsx`, routed at `/checkout/success` and `/checkout/failure` in `App.tsx`; success page refetches the order via React Query (poll briefly until `paid`, since the webhook may lag the redirect).
- Cart sync: rework `src/store/cartStore.ts` to sync with the server cart via the currently unused `cartApi` for authenticated users — local optimistic updates backed by `GET/POST/PUT/DELETE /api/cart...`; merge the local persisted cart into the server cart on login.
- Add `ordersApi.pay(id)` helper in `src/services/api.ts`.

### Relevant files / endpoints
- `packages/payments/src/*` (provider interface, factory, mock — scaffold on branch `claude/app-review-purchase-system-bp8j0l`; new `MercadoPagoProvider`)
- `packages/database/src/models/Order.ts`, `packages/database/src/models/index.ts`, new `packages/database/src/models/Payment.ts` + migration
- `packages/api/src/app.ts`, `packages/api/src/routes/orders.ts`, `packages/api/src/controllers/orderController.ts`, new `paymentController.ts`, `packages/api/.env.example`
- `packages/app/src/store/cartStore.ts`, `packages/app/src/services/api.ts`, `packages/app/src/pages/Checkout.tsx`, `packages/app/src/App.tsx`
- Endpoints: `POST /api/orders/:id/pay` [auth], `POST /api/webhooks/payments` (public, signature-verified), existing `POST /api/orders`, `GET /api/orders/:id`, `GET/POST/PUT/DELETE /api/cart...`

### Implementation notes
- Use Mercado Pago's official Node SDK (or plain HTTPS calls) with `MERCADOPAGO_ACCESS_TOKEN`; test with sandbox credentials and Checkout Pro test cards/Pix.
- Store every raw webhook payload in `Payment.raw` (JSONB) for auditability and reprocessing.
- Stock handling: decrement stock when the order is created (existing behaviour, order `pending`); restore it on rejection/expiry/cancellation — never on duplicate webhook deliveries.
- Refunds: map provider `refunded` events to `Payment.status = refunded` and `Order.status = cancelled` (admin-triggered refunds are out of scope for this issue).
- Keep all Mercado Pago-specific code inside `packages/payments`; `api/` must only import the `PaymentProvider` interface and factory.

## Priority
P1 — the store cannot actually take money today; this is the core purchase flow, but the site itself is not broken (no P0).

## Labels
`feature`, `cross-module`, `p1`

body:
Tracking issue for the remediation work that came out of an adversarial review of the Stripe payment integration (single entry point: `PaymentClient.scala`, raw WSClient, no Stripe SDK).

## Verdict
The third-party payment feature is an **unfinished MVP**:
- **Does it work today?** The flat-subscription path (`costPerMonth` only) probably works; the metered / pay-per-request path is broken on recent Stripe accounts; several functions are stubs.
- **Is it up to date?** No — it uses the legacy usage-based billing APIs Stripe removed in `2025-03-31.basil`, and no `Stripe-Version` is pinned.
- **What's missing?** Webhooks (reliable confirmation), idempotency, failure/cancellation handling, Stripe-side cleanup, and any test coverage.
- **Security:** the Stripe secret key leaks into the SPA payload served to the browser.

## Sub-issues (suggested order)
- [ ] #1148 — 🔴 Security: Stripe secret key leaked into the SPA payload (`toUiPayload`)
- [ ] #1149 — 🔴 Migrate metered billing to the Billing Meters API + pin `Stripe-Version`
- [ ] #1150 — 🟠 Add signed webhooks for reliable payment confirmation
- [ ] #1151 — 🟠 Implement `stopPayment` + fix billing portal legal URLs
- [ ] #1152 — 🟡 Harden `PaymentClient` (idempotency, bugs, currencies, 429)
- [ ] #1153 — 🟡 Test coverage for the payment flow (mock `api.stripe.com`)

## Related existing issues
- #1130 — Reconcile enabled subscriptions with Otoroshi: Daikoku as the source of truth (overlaps with webhooks #1150).
- #1109 — Subscription deletion: offload heavy work to the queue job (overlaps with `stopPayment` cleanup #1151 and the additive usage-sync double-count noted in `QueueJob.scala:508`).
- #786 — Extend the portal subscription model beyond API key delivery (broader payment/portal context).
